summary: Apart from ECOWAS citizens, who enter freely, visitors to Burkina Faso need a visa arranged in advance through a Burkinabè embassy or the government's online visa service, and most Western governments currently advise against all travel because of widespread jihadist violence.

currencyLimits.text: Declare large amounts of foreign currency on arrival. The CFA franc is not freely convertible outside the West African monetary union; confirm current thresholds with customs.

payments.text: Burkina Faso runs on cash and mobile money (Orange Money, Moov). Cards work only at a handful of hotels in Ouagadougou, and ATMs outside the two main cities are unreliable.

safety.text: Most Western governments advise against all travel to Burkina Faso. Jihadist groups contest large parts of the country, attacks and kidnapping occur including on main roads, and a state of emergency covers many regions; the situation can change quickly.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Burkina Faso Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: November to February is the dry, relatively cool season — though any visit currently needs to be weighed against do-not-travel advisories; March to May is extremely hot.

idp.text: Burkina Faso is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Burkina Faso is a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1968 Vienna one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1949 Geneva version. A permit issued under the 1968 Vienna Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Burkina Faso yet.

tips.text: The US, UK and most EU governments advise against all travel to Burkina Faso — if travel is unavoidable, arrange professional security support and keep plans flexible.
Overland routes and border areas are the most dangerous — attacks and IEDs occur on main roads, and several land borders are closed or restricted; fly in and out of Ouagadougou if you must go.
The yellow fever certificate is checked on arrival. Carry the yellow card with your passport.
Apply for your visa well in advance — requirements and fees differ between embassies, and some ask for an invitation letter or hotel booking.
Bring enough CFA franc cash or euros to exchange — card payments are rare even in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Burkina Faso?
faq.answer: ECOWAS citizens enter freely without a visa. Everyone else needs a visa arranged before travel, through a Burkinabè embassy or the government's online visa service — do not count on obtaining one at the border.

faq.question: Is Burkina Faso safe to visit?
faq.answer: For most travelers, no at present. The US, UK and most European governments advise against all travel due to terrorism and kidnapping risk across much of the country, including areas close to Ouagadougou. Check current advisories before making any plans.

faq.question: Does Burkina Faso have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Burkina Faso has introduced an online visa service, but its availability and coverage vary. Many travelers still apply through an embassy. Confirm the current channel with the nearest Burkinabè mission before applying, and avoid unofficial visa websites.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Burkina Faso?
faq.answer: Yes. A yellow fever certificate is required from all travelers aged 9 months and over, whatever country you arrive from.

faq.question: Can ECOWAS citizens enter Burkina Faso without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes — citizens of ECOWAS member states enter freely under the Community's free-movement protocol for stays of up to 90 days, though border security checks are extensive given the current situation.
